Moving in Los Angeles

How much do movers cost in Los Angeles, from the Valley to the Westside?

Enter two Los Angeles ZIP codes in the calculator below to see how much do movers cost in Los Angeles for your apartment or house.

20+ years in the moving business

  • Home or apartment

Where are you moving?

Two ZIP codes give us the distance and the type of move.

Estimator's noteShort moves are usually billed by the hour for the crew and truck. Long moves are priced by the weight of your things and the distance. Your ZIP codes decide which applies.

Your price shows before we ask for any contact details.

Local movers cost $280–$740 for a studio and $720–$1,800 for a 2-bedroom home moved 10 road miles, on an off-peak date with no stairs or extras, and each mover adds $50–$75 an hour to the crew's rate. That is the baseline answer to how much do movers cost in Los Angeles. Within LA, the billed drive between your two addresses, hillside access and apartment elevators push most moves above it.

How much do movers cost in Los Angeles by the hour?

A move from one Los Angeles address to another is billed by the hour, for the crew and the truck together. A studio or 1-bedroom usually takes 2 movers at $100–$150 an hour, a 2-bedroom home 3 movers at $150–$225 an hour, and a 3-bedroom house 4 movers at $200–$300 an hour. A 2-bedroom job usually runs four and a half to eight hours, so the hours matter as much as the rate when you work out how much do movers cost in Los Angeles.

Those rates come from the national rate table behind the calculator, not from Los Angeles quotes. Most of the city's households rent, most homes are in apartment buildings, and most have 1 or 2 bedrooms, as the home-size panel below shows, so the typical LA move is a 2- or 3-mover job in a building with stairs or an elevator.

California also caps what an hourly mover may charge. The Bureau of Household Goods and Services (BHGS) publishes the Maximum Rate Tariff 4, known as Max 4, which sets maximum hourly rates and the rules for counting billable time. It also allows higher overtime rates when you ask for service at a time the mover must pay its crew overtime, so an evening or holiday start can change how much do movers cost in Los Angeles for the same job.

Double drive time: the LA rule that bills the freeway twice

Here is the rule that most separates an LA bill from one in another state. Under BHGS's Max 4 tariff, the time charged on an hourly move is the loading time, the unloading time and double the driving time from your old address to your new one. A 40-minute drive from Silver Lake to Santa Monica is billed as 80 minutes. If the crew needs more than one trip, the first trip is billed at double the driving time and the later trips at their actual time.

That makes traffic part of how much do movers cost in Los Angeles. The 10, the 405 and the 101 can turn a short distance into a long drive, and every minute of it is counted twice. Moving at midday, or early on a weekend morning when the mover's rates allow it, can cut the billed drive more than any other change you make. The calculator counts the drive as crew time, so enter both ZIP codes to price the real route.

Hillsides, canyons and apartment buildings

Los Angeles has some of the hardest access of any big city. In the Hollywood Hills, Laurel Canyon, Silver Lake and Echo Park, homes sit on narrow, winding streets and up long flights of outdoor steps. A full-size truck may not get up the hill at all, so the crew shuttles loads in a smaller truck, and each extra trip is billed time. Describe the street and the steps when you ask for an estimate, or the hours will run past the range for how much do movers cost in Los Angeles.

Apartment buildings bring their own costs. Many want a reserved elevator and a set move window, and some charge a move-in or move-out fee or ask for a certificate of insurance from your mover. Underground garages often have too little clearance for a moving truck, so the crew carries everything from the street. Ask the building manager for the rules in writing and pass them to each mover before it prices the move.

Curb space, LADOT signs and the cities inside LA

A truck parked at the door saves the long carry that adds to how much do movers cost in Los Angeles. Within the City of Los Angeles, moving companies can order temporary tow-away signs from LADOT to hold curb space for the truck, and the local rules panel below gives the lead time and how to request them. Ask your mover whether it orders the signs, and whether their cost is on the estimate.

Not every LA address is in the City of Los Angeles. Santa Monica, West Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Culver City and Burbank are separate cities with their own parking rules, so check with the city at each end of the move.

Pricing a Koreatown-to-Santa Monica apartment move

Say you're moving a 1-bedroom apartment in a Koreatown high-rise to a second-floor walk-up in Santa Monica. On baseline terms the move costs $380–$960, with 2 movers at $100–$150 an hour. Here is where how much do movers cost in Los Angeles rises above that for this move:

  • the drive west on the 10 is billed at double its time, and more at rush hour;
  • the Koreatown building's freight elevator has to be booked, and any wait for it is crew time;
  • the stairs at the Santa Monica end add carry time, which the calculator adds for you;
  • a 6 p.m. start you asked for may fall into overtime;
  • a packing service for 1 bedroom adds $300–$650.

Book a midday start, reserve the elevator, pack the boxes yourself and the same move lands near the baseline. Put your own date, stairs and ZIP codes into the calculator above to see the range move with each choice.

Labor-only help and smaller jobs

If you drive a rental truck yourself, you can hire the lifting alone. Labor-only help costs $80–$130 an hour for 2 movers, or $320–$910 in all to load and unload, off peak and with no extras. A 15-foot rental truck costs $29.95–$30.00 a day plus $0.69–$2.49 per mile in town, by published rental prices. With no truck on the mover's clock, double drive time drops out, and for many renters that is the cheapest answer to how much do movers cost in Los Angeles.

Moving a sofa, a bed frame and a dresser rather than a whole home? A move of 1 to 3 items costs $180–$590 for 10 road miles, off peak with no stairs or extras.

Getting a firm figure for how much do movers cost in Los Angeles

  1. Run your ZIP codes, home size, date and stairs through the calculator above. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to see the price.
  2. Check each mover's household mover license with BHGS's license search before you book.
  3. Ask every mover how it bills drive time, overtime, stairs and long carries, and get each answer in writing.
  4. Get written estimates from two or three licensed movers for the same inventory, date and start time, and compare them line by line.

BHGS's consumer guide to household moving explains the rest of your rights on a move within California. Once you have two or three written estimates beside the calculator's range, you know how much do movers cost in Los Angeles for your own home, route and start time.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • Of 10 major cities, Riverside is the nearest to Los Angeles, 70 road miles away: a 2-bedroom home move between them runs $970–$2,300 off peak.
  • With 3 movers, a 2-bedroom home move takes about 4–6.5 hours on site: $720–$1,800 off peak at 10 road miles.
  • Anyone who is paid to move household goods entirely within California is required to have a household mover license from the Bureau of Household Goods and Services.
  • Guides put a 2-bedroom home at about 40–90 boxes.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 6 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • The most common home in Los Angeles has 2 bedrooms: 31% of homes, against 25% across the US.
  • Order LADOT tow-away signs 10 business days before the move (LADOT).
  • Hourly moves within California are billed for loading, unloading and double the driving time between your two addresses.
  • Freeway traffic on that drive is billed twice, so the time of day you move can matter as much as the distance.
  • California's maximum rate tariff allows overtime rates, so ask each mover whether your date and start time fall into overtime.
  • Hillside streets and apartment buildings add carry time and elevator waits, so describe both when you ask for an estimate.

Kitchen: what goes in which box

Plates and glasses in dish packs, canned goods and other dense things in small boxes, cookware and small appliances in medium boxes.

Living room: what goes in which box

Books in small boxes, decor in medium boxes, throw pillows and lampshades in large boxes.

Main bedroom: what goes in which box

Hanging clothes in wardrobe boxes, folded clothes in medium boxes, pillows and bedding in large boxes.

Other bedroom: what goes in which box

Hanging clothes in wardrobe boxes, folded clothes in medium boxes, pillows and bedding in large boxes.

Bathroom: what goes in which box

Toiletries in small boxes, with liquids bagged on their own.

An LA moving timeline, from estimate to keys

Much of how much do movers cost in Los Angeles is settled before moving day. Enter your date to see each task in order, from booking parking and the crew to the last walk-through.

0 of 14 done

6 weeks before

  • Check that it lists everything you told the company, and that nothing you asked for is missing.

4 weeks before

  • Label each box with its room and what's inside.

  • If another company will do the job, get its name and check it too.

2 weeks before

  • Keep the backup apart from the devices on moving day.

  • A clear answer helps you plan the day, and check the bill if you pay by the hour.

  • A sketch with each room named lets the crew put things in place on the first trip.

1 week before

  • Chargers, basic tools, toilet paper, cleaning supplies, snacks and a change of clothes.

  • Ask the building or the city whether you need a permit or cones.

  • The truck may block a driveway or part of the street for a while.

The day before

  • Tape a sign on it, or gather it in one room, so it isn't loaded by mistake.

Moving day

  • Look high and low: top shelves, under sinks, the attic and the garage.

  • FMCSA's advice: if you can't be there, ask someone you know to act for you.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

After the move

  • If you're on active duty in the Armed Forces and moved under a military order for a permanent change of station, the IRS says you may be able to deduct moving costs you weren't reimbursed for.

    Source: Internal Revenue Service

  • Send photos and a list of what's damaged or missing as soon as you find it.

LADOT sign rules for an LA moving truck

Where the truck parks changes how much do movers cost in Los Angeles, because a long carry is billed time. Here is the City rule for reserving curb space for the truck, with its source.

Order LADOT tow-away signs 10 business days before the move

LADOT's Temporary Tow Away signs set temporary parking restrictions for moving companies to accommodate a moving van or delivery truck. Request them by phone before 12 noon on a weekday, at least 10 business days ahead, not counting weekends or City holidays. The signs are posted two days before the event.

Source: LADOT, checked 28 October 2026

Questions

How much do movers cost in Los Angeles, from the Valley to the Westside? FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

How much do movers cost in Los Angeles for a full day?

Multiply the crew's hourly rate by the hours. A 3-mover crew for a 2-bedroom home costs $150–$225 an hour, so an eight-hour day is eight times that, before packing or extras. If the day runs past the crew's regular hours, ask whether overtime applies, because it changes how much do movers cost in Los Angeles for the last hours.

Is a weekend move in Los Angeles more expensive?

Often, yes. Weekends book up first, and California's Max 4 tariff allows overtime rates when you ask for service at a time the mover must pay its crew overtime. A weekday midday slot avoids both, and it usually means less freeway traffic, which matters when the drive is billed at double its time.

How much should you tip each mover in Los Angeles?

Tipping is up to you and isn't part of how much do movers cost in Los Angeles on the bill. Moving guides suggest $10.00–$20.00 per mover for a job of up to 4 hours and $20.00–$65.00 per mover for a full day. Tip toward the top for hillside steps or a long carry from the street.

What extra charges show up on a short Los Angeles move?

Ask about a minimum number of hours, double drive time between your addresses, stairs, a long carry from the truck, elevator waits, packing materials and any overtime. On a short job these can be a large share of how much do movers cost in Los Angeles, so get each one written into the estimate before moving day.

How can you spot a moving scam in Los Angeles?

Check that the company holds a household mover license from BHGS, and be wary of an estimate given without anyone seeing your belongings, or one far cheaper than every other. BHGS also warns against paying a large deposit. A licensed mover will put its rates and charges in writing before the move.
